title: Command Pallet Multiple Displays
author: xtremewaianae
summary: Command Palette displays GDI device names rather than Windows Identify ordinals, explaining the numbering mismatch. The reported physical movement remains unproven after a shipped topology fix and needs a focused dock reconnect capture.

status.label: Placement regression needs proof
status.detail: The cosmetic numbering mismatch has existing ownership; only a before-and-after physical placement capture can establish a remaining docking regression.

next_action.label: Request focused dock reconnect evidence
next_action.reason: Identify whether the enabled dock configuration changes during the laptop-to-hub topology transition.

judgment.rationale: The attachment confirms a GDI-name versus Windows Identify-number mismatch, but that presentation difference does not prove why the Dock physically moved. The diagnostic version already includes the recent topology-change fix, so a controlled transition is necessary before proposing another implementation.
evidence: The reporter supplied a screenshot, diagnostic ZIP, and a laptop-only to multi-display-hub scenario.
The diagnostic inventory records GDI names DISPLAY1, DISPLAY2, DISPLAY3, and DISPLAY21.
MonitorService.FormatDisplayName can turn a GDI device name such as `\\.\DISPLAY21` into Display 21.
Issue 49295 already tracks the display-number mismatch.
PR 49814 addressed docking/topology changes and the diagnostic Command Palette build includes that change.
The diagnostic lacks the persisted MonitorConfigs and logs for the topology transition.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a precise laptop-only to hub-connected Dock placement capture, including the enabled physical monitor before and after reconnection.

fix_assessment.rationale: PR 49814 is a merged topology-change fix and Issue 49295 owns the label mismatch. Neither proves that this report's remaining physical-movement symptom is resolved, so new implementation work would be speculative.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette presents volatile GDI display names as labels that differ from Windows Settings, while the claimed dock movement needs transition-time evidence.
known_information: The reporter used PowerToys 0.100.2 from Microsoft Store and supplied a screenshot and diagnostic archive.
Windows Identify showed displays 1 through 4 while Command Palette showed labels 1, 2, 3, and 21.
The archive identifies the laptop panel as GDI device `\\.\DISPLAY3`.
Command Palette formats this GDI name as a display label when no friendly name is available.
Issue 49295 is an open report of the same numbering mismatch.
The archive's Command Palette build includes PR 49814's topology-change fix.
inferences: GDI-name formatting explains the numbering mismatch but does not establish incorrect monitor selection.
A remaining physical move could be a configuration-reassociation problem, but the archive cannot identify which reconciliation path ran.
The existing topology change fix may already cover the movement symptom; a controlled retest is required.
issue_context.analysis: The report already supplies the physical-to-GDI mapping, so asking again for monitor numbering would be redundant. The action targets only the evidence that distinguishes a cosmetic label issue from a reproducible Dock placement regression.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, screenshot, diagnostic archive, labels, and timeline.
Inspected MonitorService.FormatDisplayName, DockMonitorConfigViewModel, DockSettingsPage, DockWindowManager, and MonitorConfigReconciler.
Reviewed PR 49814, Issue 48516, Issue 49295, and relevant Windows monitor-device documentation.

information_gaps.information: Before-and-after physical monitor placement and per-monitor Dock toggle state across a laptop-only to hub-connected transition.
information_gaps.why_needed: Shows whether the Dock only appears mislabeled or its enabled monitor configuration actually changes.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Enable the Dock only on the physical laptop panel, capture Windows Identify and Command Palette's per-monitor toggles, reconnect the hub, then capture both the toggles and the physical screen where the Dock appears.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic captured immediately after a verified enabled-monitor change or physical move.
information_gaps.why_needed: The supplied archive does not capture the transition or persisted monitor configuration.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If the enabled monitor changes or the Dock moves after reconnecting the hub, add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

actions.label: Request dock reconnect evidence

comment.body: Thanks for the screenshot and diagnostic ZIP. The archive identifies the laptop panel as the GDI device `\\.\DISPLAY3`; that identifier is not the same numbering system shown by Windows Settings, and the label mismatch is already tracked in #49295. The archive also shows a Command Palette build containing the docking/topology change from #49814. To determine whether a placement regression remains, please connect all monitors, enable the Dock only on the physical laptop panel, and capture the per-monitor toggles and physical Dock location before and after disconnecting and reconnecting the hub. If the enabled monitor changes or the Dock moves, please add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately afterward.
